timeline.tweet: I was diagnosed with dysphoria the same year I was diagnosed with depression. Psychiatrist told me that if I took hormones, I probably would be 'happy enough' to stop anti-depressants within six months. I was fifteen.

I feel that. I still have that discomfort. But I think I approached it more so as I approached my eating disorder. In my brain, my body looks ‘wrong’ for a multitude of reasons. I just simply don’t think that’s a state of being one arrives at without societal influence.

When I was thirteen, I came to the realization that I was a lesbian after a year of horrific bullying, several years struggling with depression & PTSD, and I hated myself. I hated being a woman, I hated being the victim of homophobia. I hated who I was.

It did end up ‘helping’ my depression in the sense that it completely made my mind numb. I felt so disconnected from having any sense of self.Couldn’t feel anything the way I used to, and even a year later, I can still feel the effects of it in my body.
